evidence.note: Bury's introduction/prefatory treatment rejects the First Letter and highlights conflicts with the more credible Sicilian narrative.
Wohl surveys the authenticity debate and notes that modern acceptance of the collection commonly excludes Letter I (and XII).

rationale: The First Letter is rejected by modern scholarship with exceptional consistency. Bury treats it as spurious, and Victoria Wohl notes that modern defenses of the Epistles commonly exclude Letter I even where much of the collection is accepted. The classification records authorship judgment only; the letter remains part of the historical Platonic corpus tradition.
